laws.title: Conformance Required
laws.content:
A. Fixtures: The use of any luminaire not in conformance with this chapter is prohibited. This applies to both public and private outdoor luminaire installation.

B. Mercury Vapor Lamp Or Luminaire: The outdoor installation or use of any mercury vapor lamp or mercury vapor luminaire is prohibited.

C. Inspection: The village reserves the right to conduct a postinstallation nighttime inspection to verify compliance with ordinance requirements, and to require remedial action at no expense to the village, if appropriate. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005)

laws.title: Shielding
laws.content: Except as otherwise provided, or in subsection 8-3-1B of this chapter, all outdoor luminaires shall be shielded in such a manner that light rays emitted by the luminaire, whether directly from the lamp or indirectly from the luminaire, are restricted to regions below an angle fifteen degrees (15°) beneath the horizontal plane running through the lowest point on the luminaire where light is emitted. No significant intensity of light shall be emitted from the luminaire horizontally, nor above the horizon, nor above the region defined above. In general, all outdoor lighting shall be downward directed, except where specified otherwise in this chapter. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005)

laws.title: Light Pollution and Light Trespass
laws.content:
A. Shielding Required: Following the effective date hereof, only shielded outdoor luminaires which conform to the requirement of section 8-3-3 of this chapter may be newly installed or modified, except for lamp replacement but only of the same type and of the same or lesser wattage. B. Installed Public Or Private Lighting: Only fully shielded, low pressure sodium or fully shielded high pressure sodium outdoor luminaires may be newly installed to provide illumination for public and private streets and for areas designated for public and private parking. This includes both pole and wall mounted luminaires. C. Time Limits For Illumination; Exceptions: All outdoor luminaires maintained on public or private property, whether installed before or after the effective date hereof, shall be turned off between eleven o'clock (11:00) P.M. (local time) and sunrise, except when used for: 1. Commercial And Industrial Uses: Commercial and industrial uses (such as sales, assembly and repair areas) where business is conducted after eleven o'clock (11:00) P.M., but only while the business is open to the public; 2. Advertising Signs: Illuminated advertising signs on the premises of a business while it is open to the public; 3. Security Lighting: Per IESNA guidelines, lighting necessary for security purposes or to illuminate walkways or roadways; or 4. Recreational Use: Recreational use that continues after eleven o'clock (11:00) P.M., but only for so long as such use continues. D. High Intensity Beams: The outdoor operation of searchlights, lasers with greater than five (5) milliwatts visible output power, or other high intensity beams is prohibited. E. Public Safety: For pedestrian and vehicular safety, glare shall not be observable (outside the originating property limits for private installation) at an angle greater than seventy five degrees (75°) from the nadir of the vertical axis of the light source. The definition of "glare" in the context of light trespass is more stringent, given below in subsection G of this section. F. Maximum Luminance: No permanently mounted luminaire shall employ a lamp rated greater than one hundred fifty (150) watts. Temporary use "task lighting" luminaires may exceed these limits by a factor of four (4), but for no more than thirty (30) days in a given calendar year. Also, no more than the equivalent of two hundred fifty (250) watts per acre of illumination from conforming luminaires may be employed on any property. G. Light Trespass: All public and private lighting shall be shielded and/or directed in such a manner that it does not spill over into neighboring premises so as to interfere with the peaceful enjoyment of these premises. Light trespass can only exist if there is a complaint. In cases of unresolved disagreement, a formal complaint may be filed by the aggrieved party to the village codes enforcement officials, who will then make a determination and take appropriate actions. Even though a luminaire may be legally installed and operated as given above, it is possible for any luminaire to create a light trespass situation. For purposes of evaluation, "light trespass" shall be defined as follows: 1. Light falling onto nearby residential property, bright enough to create a shadow easily seen on a dark, moonless night; and/or 2. Nuisance glare, where the illuminating source lamp or its reflection can be seen with significant intensity by a person standing off premises. The provisions of this section apply to all luminaires. For the purposes of light trespass, a luminaire is no longer considered newly installed after one year from the date of installation or modification in the absence of complaint. In the event of a formal complaint regarding an existing off street luminaire, the complaining party(ies) shall be financially responsible for any modifications found necessary to eliminate the light trespass. For newly installed lighting, the owner may elect to obtain written agreement that the lighting does not constitute light trespass from the owners of neighboring properties. If such agreement is obtained, a later complaint cannot be filed by these persons except as defined under the existing luminaires clause, or if the luminaire fails to meet the requirements elsewhere in this chapter. If a contractor or public utility installs an off street luminaire, they are obliged to ensure that the owner warrants that the luminaire does not produce light trespass, and/or that the owners of the neighboring properties have in writing agreed to the installation of the luminaire. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005) 8-3-5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS: A. Flashing Lights: The use of flashing, rotating or pulsating lights in/on any outdoor sign or other lighting device is prohibited. This provision shall not apply to flashing, rotating or pulsating lights intended to warn of hazards and danger, nor to decorator lights as given to subsection 8-3-7A of this chapter. B. Operation: No luminaire may be operated in such manner as to constitute a hazard or danger to persons, or to safe vehicular operation. C. Signs And Billboards: Illuminating fixtures for advertising or other signs shall be such that the illumination is confined to the area of the sign or billboard. Under no conditions may signs or billboards be illuminated from below. Any such illuminating fixture shall be placed above its respective sign or billboard such that the secondary (specular) reflected light from the surface of the sign or billboard is directed down toward the ground. D. Motion Detector Security Lights: Motion detector security lights, which are normally "off" and which are activated "on" for less than four (4) minutes occasionally when motion is detected, are exempt from strict control of emission angles as defined in section 8-3-3 of this chapter, but are not exempt from subsection B of this section, and subsection 8-3-4G, "Light Trespass", of this chapter. E. Outdoor Recreational Facilities: Outdoor recreational facilities designed for specifically scheduled sporting events are exempt from the specific shielding requirements of section 8-3-3 of this chapter. In its place, lighting for outdoor recreational facilities shall be so designed, installed and operated as to confine at least ninety percent (90%) of the illumination to the recreational area. Recreational facility fixtures shall be on elevated poles or structures so that illumination is directed downward. No significant intensity of light may extend above a horizontal plane from the lighting fixture. Illumination from recreational facility fixtures shall be shielded to minimize glare extending toward roadways or other places where impairment of motorists' vision might cause hazard. All such recreational lighting shall be extinguished at the close of the recreational activity. F. U.S. Flags; Mounted Objects: In the case of pole mounted U.S. flags that cannot be easily illuminated with down lighting, upward lighting may be used only in the form of one narrow cone spotlight which confines the illumination to the flag. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005) **8-3-6: NONCONFORMING FIXTURES; GRANDFATHER PROVISION:** Outdoor lighting fixtures preexisting and legally installed and operative before the effective date hereof are exempt from the requirements of this chapter for the life of the preexisting fixture. This exemption does not apply to the requirements of section 8-3-5 or subsection 8-3-4G of this chapter, which shall be binding on "grandfathered" fixtures beginning one year from the effective date hereof. Whenever a preexisting nonconforming luminaire is replaced or moved, the replacement thenceforth shall meet the requirements of this chapter. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005) **8-3-7: SPECIAL EXEMPTIONS:** A. Decorator Lights: Decorator lamps smaller than one-half (0.5) watt rating may be used in any desired string length year round, but are still subject to light trespass restrictions given in subsection 8-3-4G of this chapter. B. Temporary Exemption Request: Request for temporary exemption from the provisions of this chapter may be submitted to the village board of trustees in written form describing the reason for the request and the nature of the request. If approved and granted in writing by an authorized representative of the village board of trustees, such exemption shall be in force for not more than thirty (30) days. Request for a maximum of one 15-day renewal may be made in similar manner. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005) **8-3-8: EFFECT ON OTHER CODES; CONFLICTS:** The provisions of this chapter are intended to supplement other applicable codes and requirements. Compliance with all applicable provisions of building, electrical and other codes must be observed. In the event of a conflict between the requirements of this chapter and other requirements, the more stringent requirement shall apply. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005) **8-3-9: PENALTY:** Violations of this chapter shall be subject to the general penalty provisions contained in section 1-4-1 of this code. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005) **8-3-10: OUTDOOR LIGHTING ADVISORY COMMITTEE ESTABLISHED:** In order to evaluate compliance in new installations and in cases of dispute, there is hereby established an "outdoor lighting advisory committee" to be appointed by the mayor with approval of a majority of all members of the governing body to consist of not less than three (3) persons. At the request of the village, this volunteer resource board will advise the village council, the village manager, and/or the planning and zoning officer on questions of interpretation of this chapter, provide guidelines for new construction and installations. In addition, this advisory committee will provide outdoor lighting resources and information materials to the village for distribution to the community. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005)

CHAPTER 4

FIRE CODE

SECTION: 8-4-1: Fire Code Adopted 8-4-2: Fire Limits Established 8-4-3: Penalty 8-4-4: Life Safety Code **8-4-1: FIRE CODE ADOPTED:** There is hereby adopted for the purpose of prescribing regulation governing conditions hazardous to life and property from fire or explosion, the code, standards and requirement adopted under chapter 59A, article 52 of the New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978 comp. as amended and title 10, chapter 25 of the New Mexico administration code. (Ord. 328, 8-10-2004) **8-4-2: FIRE LIMITS ESTABLISHED:** The fire limits of the village shall hereafter be and include the following: Within the village limits. (Ord. 328, 8-10-2004) **8-4-3: PENALTY:** Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be subject to penalty as provided in section 1-4-1 of this code and each day that any building is in process of erection or is allowed to stand after completion, shall constitute a separate and distinct offense. (Ord. 328, 8-10-2004) **8-4-4: LIFE SAFETY CODE:** There is hereby adopted for purposes of prescribing regulations governing conditions hazardous to life the code and standards adopted under section 60-13-44, New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978 comp. as amended and as adopted under title 14 of the New Mexico administration code. (Ord. 328, 8-10-2004)
**CHAPTER 5** **FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTION**
**SECTION:** 8-5-1: Statutory Authorization 8-5-2: Findings Of Fact 8-5-3: Statement Of Purpose 8-5-4: Methods Of Reducing Flood Losses 8-5-5: Definitions 8-5-6: Lands To Which This Chapter Applies 8-5-7: Basis For Establishing Areas Of Special Flood Hazard 8-5-8: Establishment Of Development Permit 8-5-9: Compliance 8-5-10: Abrogation And Greater Restrictions 8-5-11: Interpretation 8-5-12: Warning And Disclaimer Of Liability 8-5-13: Designation Of Floodplain Administrator 8-5-14: Duties And Responsibilities Of Floodplain Administrator 8-5-15: Permit Procedures 8-5-16: Variance Procedures 8-5-17: General Standards For Flood Hazard Reduction 8-5-18: Standards For Subdivision Proposals 8-5-19: Severability 8-5-20: Penalties For Noncompliance **8-5-1: STATUTORY AUTHORIZATION:** The legislature of the state of New Mexico has in chapter 3, articles 18 and 41 New Mexico Statutes Annotated, 1978 compilation, authorized local governmental units to adopt regulations designed to minimize flood losses. Therefore, the governing body of the village of Cloudcroft does ordain as follows. (Ord. 341, 11-27-2006) **8-5-2: FINDINGS OF FACT:** A. The flood hazard areas of the village of Cloudcroft are subject to periodic inundation, which results in loss of life and property, health and safety hazards, disruption of commerce and governmental services, and extraordinary public expenditures for flood protection and relief, all of which adversely affect the public's health, safety and general welfare. B. These flood losses are created by the cumulative effect of obstructions in floodplains which causes an increase in flood heights and velocities, and by the occupancy of flood hazard areas by uses vulnerable to floods and hazardous to other lands because they are inadequately elevated, floodproofed or otherwise protected from flood damage. (Ord. 341, 11-27-2006) **8-5-3: STATEMENT OF PURPOSE:** It is the purpose of this chapter to promote the public health, safety and general welfare and to minimize public and private losses due to flood conditions in specific areas by provisions designed to: A. Protect human life and health; B. Minimize expenditure of public money for costly flood control projects; C. Minimize the need for rescue and relief efforts associated with flooding and generally undertaken at the expense of the general public; D. Minimize prolonged business interruptions; E. Minimize damage to public facilities and utilities such as water and gas mains, electric, telephone and sewer lines, streets and bridges located in floodplains; F. Help maintain a stable tax base by providing for the sound use and development of flood prone areas in such a manner as to minimize future flood blight areas; and G. Ensure that potential buyers are notified that property is in a flood area. (Ord. 341, 11-27-2006)

laws.title: Methods of Reducing Flood Losses
Variance Procedures
laws.content:
A. The appeal board as established by the community shall hear and render judgment on requests for variances from the requirements of this chapter.

B. The appeal board shall hear and render judgment on an appeal only when it is alleged there is an error in any requirement, decision or determination made by the floodplain administrator in the enforcement or administration of this chapter.

C. Any person or persons aggrieved by the decision of the appeal board may appeal such decision in the courts of competent jurisdiction.

D. The floodplain administrator shall maintain a record of all actions involving an appeal and shall report variances to the federal emergency management agency upon request.

E. Variances may be issued for the reconstruction, rehabilitation or restoration of structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places or the State Inventory of Historic Places, without regard to the procedures set forth in the remainder of this chapter.

F. Variances may be issued for new construction and substantial improvements to be erected on a lot of one-half (1/2) acre or less in size contiguous to and surrounded by lots with existing structures constructed below the base flood level, providing the relevant factors of this chapter have been fully considered. As the lot size increases beyond the one-half (1/2) acre, the technical justification required for issuing the variance increases.

G. Upon consideration of the factors noted above and the intent of this chapter, the appeal board may attach such conditions to the granting of variances as it deems necessary to further the purpose and objectives of this chapter (section 8-5-3 of this chapter).

H. Variances shall not be issued within any designated floodway if any increase in flood levels during the base flood discharge would result.

I. Variances may be issued for the repair or rehabilitation of historic structures upon a determination that the proposed repair or rehabilitation will not preclude the structure’s continued designation as a historic structure and the variance is the minimum necessary to preserve the historic character and design of the structure.

J. Prerequisites for granting variances:

1. Variances shall only be issued upon a determination that the variance is the minimum necessary, considering the flood hazard, to afford relief.

2. Variances shall only be issued upon: a) showing a good and sufficient cause; b) a determination that failure to grant
the variance would result in exceptional hardship to the applicant; and c) a determination that the granting of a variance will not result in increased flood heights, additional threats to public safety, extraordinary public expense, create nuisances, cause fraud on or victimization of the public, or conflict with existing local laws or ordinances.

3. Any applicant to whom a variance is granted shall be given written notice that the structure will be permitted to be built with the lowest floor elevation below the base flood elevation and that the cost of flood insurance will be commensurate with the increased risk resulting from the reduced lowest floor elevation.

K. Variances may be issued by a community for new construction and substantial improvements and for other development necessary for the conduct of a functionally dependent use provided that: 1) the criteria outlined in subsections A through I of this section are met, and 2) the structure or other development is protected by methods that minimize flood damages during the base flood and create no additional threats to public safety. (Ord. 341, 11-27-2006)

laws.title: General Standards for Flood Hazard Reduction
Standards for Subdivision Proposals
laws.content:
A. All subdivision proposals including the placement of manufactured home parks and subdivisions shall be consistent with this chapter.

B. All proposals for the development of subdivisions including the placement of manufactured home parks and subdivisions shall meet development permit requirements of this chapter.

C. All subdivision proposals including the placement of manufactured home parks and subdivisions shall have adequate drainage provided to reduce exposure to flood hazards.

D. All subdivision proposals including the placement of manufactured home parks and subdivisions shall have public utilities and facilities such as sewer, gas, electrical and water systems located and constructed to minimize or eliminate flood damage. (Ord. 341, 11-27-2006)

laws.title: Penalties for Noncompliance
laws.content:
No structure or land shall hereafter be constructed, located, extended, converted or altered without full compliance with the terms of this chapter and other applicable regulations. Violation of the provisions of this chapter by failure to comply with any of its requirements (including violations of conditions and safeguards established in connection with conditions) shall constitute a misdemeanor. Any person who violates this chapter or fails to comply with any of its requirements shall upon conviction thereof be fined not more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned for not more than ninety (90) days, or both, for each violation, and in addition shall pay all costs and expenses involved in the case. Nothing herein contained shall prevent the village of Cloudcroft from taking such other lawful action as is necessary to prevent or remedy any violation. (Ord. 341, 11-27-2006)

**TITLE 9**

**ZONING REGULATIONS**

laws.title: Conflicting Provisions
laws.content: Any provision of United States or state law, which imposes a greater duty, standard or requirement than those contained in this title, shall supersede the provisions of this code. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

laws.title: Planning and Zoning Code Enforcement Official
laws.content: There is hereby established the office of planning and zoning code enforcement official, whose duties shall be to enforce the provisions of the zoning regulations. He shall be appointed by the mayor with the consent of a majority of all members of the board of trustees. He shall examine the premises for which permits have been issued and shall make necessary inspections to see that the provisions of the law are complied with. He shall enforce all village ordinances relating to the construction, alteration, repair, removal, demolition, equipment, use and occupancy, location and maintenance of buildings and structures and setting of trailers (mobile homes), except as may otherwise be provided. He shall, when requested by the mayor or board of trustees, or the planning and zoning commission, or where the interests of the village so require, make investigations in connection with matters referred to in the zoning regulations, and make reports thereon to the appropriate entity. He shall communicate and cooperate with the state building inspectors. He shall keep careful and comprehensive records of applications, of permits issued, of inspections made, of reports rendered and of notices or orders issued, and make reports to the planning and zoning commission as requested. If a violation exists, he shall notify the responsible party or parties, by certified mail, return receipt requested, of the nature of the violation and what procedures shall be taken to correct same. Copies of the notice shall be distributed to the mayor and to the members of the planning and zoning commission. If no response is received in ten (10) days, or if immediate action is necessary, the code enforcement official shall prepare an order, for the mayor’s signature, directing the police department to issue to the violator a nontraffic citation. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003)

laws.title: Permits
laws.content:
A. Required: It shall be unlawful to construct, alter, move or demolish a structure (permanent or temporary), set a trailer (mobile home), erect a nonexempt sign, or construct a fence, without first obtaining a village building permit and a state building permit where applicable. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) B. Temporary Structure: It shall be unlawful to establish a temporary structure without first obtaining a temporary structure permit. C. Commercial Temporary Structure: No commercial temporary structures shall be allowed. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) D. Expiration Of Permit: A permit under which work has not been completed (issued a certificate of occupancy) within one year after issuance shall expire by limitation. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) E. Permit Applications: 1. An application for a permit shall be submitted in a form the planning and zoning code enforcement official may subscribe. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997; amd. Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) 2. The application shall be made by the property owner or lessee, or agent of either. If the application is made by a person other than the property owner, it shall be accompanied by a duly verified affidavit from the property owner or his agent, that the proposed work is authorized by the property owner, and that the person making the application is authorized to make the application. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) 3. The application shall contain the full names and addresses of the applicant and the owner and, if the owner is a corporate body, of its responsible officers. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) 4. The application shall include a copy of the building plans. In cases where a state building permit is required, said plans shall be identical to those submitted to the state, and the application shall include a copy of the state building permit. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) 5. The application shall include: a surveyed plot plan provided by a licensed New Mexico surveyor showing the location of the proposed structure on the lot, as well as the location of all existing structures, signs and fences that will remain on the lot; setbacks; location of water, sewer and electrical lines; location of streets and rights of way; off street parking; elevations including height of the structure from grade on each elevation; a statement of how construction materials will be disposed of; certification that the roofing material is nonflammable and the eaves will be enclosed; and such other information as may be required by the village. Applications for sign permits shall include all dimensions of the sign and, where relevant, of the structure to which it is attached; for freestanding signs, the applicant shall supply a plot plan showing the location of the sign on the property, and of all other signs and structures already existing on the property. The applicant shall also list the materials of which the sign is to be constructed and, when applicable, a description of how the sign is to be lighted. (Ord. 344, 7-10-2007) 6. All work performed under a permit shall conform to the approved application and plans and any approved amendment thereof. 7. The location of all new construction as shown on the approved plot diagram or an approved amendment thereof shall be strictly adhered to. 8. It shall be unlawful to reduce or diminish the area of a lot or plot of which a plot diagram has been filed and approved; provided, this shall not apply when the lot is reduced by reason of a street opening or widening or other public improvement. 9. The permits (village and state) shall be posted on the premises in a manner easily seen from the street until the completion of the work. 10. A certified copy of the approved plans shall be kept on the premises at all times until the work is completed. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) F. Supplemental Permit: A supplemental permit is required if a project is changed from the original permit in such a way as to increase height, decrease a setback, or increase the dimension of a sign. A supplemental permit shall be processed in the same manner as the original permit. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) G. Prior Issued Permit: Nothing in this section shall require changes in the plans, construction or designated use of a building for which a lawful permit was issued prior to October 29, 1997 (effective date of ordinance 277), or which has been otherwise lawfully authorized, and the construction of which shall have been actually begun within ninety (90) days after the provisions of the zoning regulations become effective. H. Signature Of Authorized Official: Every permit issued by the village under the provisions of the zoning regulations shall have the signature of the village clerk/treasurer or other authorized representative affixed thereto. I. Transferability: Permits are not transferable. J. Revocation: The village may revoke a permit or approval issued under the provisions of these regulations if there has been any false statement or misrepresentation as to a material fact in the application or plans on which the permit or approval was based. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) K. Special Use Permits: In extraordinary circumstances a special use permit temporarily permitting a prohibited use may be granted by the board of trustees. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) L. Application, Documentation And Fees: 1. Applicant shall submit the completed application and all supporting documentation (site plans, building plans, sketches, drawings, etc.) to the village office at least twenty four (24) hours prior to a regular or special planning and zoning commission meeting and pay the specified fee. 2. Applicant or applicant’s authorized representative shall attend the planning and zoning commission meeting at which his application appears on the agenda. (Ord. 300, 4-10-2001) M. Permit Approval: For buildings, fences, accessory buildings, signs, and demolition permits that conform to all ordinances and codes, the Village Clerk-Treasurer or his designee shall issue the appropriate permit within three (3) working days of receiving the completed application and fee, except that the Clerk- Treasurer or his designee shall delay issuing the Village permit until a copy of the State permit, if one is required, is submitted. Permits approved by the Clerk-Treasurer or his designee shall be summarized and included in the minutes of the next meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) N. Appeals, Variances And Zone Changes: 1. An applicant for a permit that is not recommended for approval by the Village Clerk-Treasurer or designee may modify the application, appeal to the Planning and Zoning Commission, or request a variance or a zone change. 2. If applicant or applicant’s authorized representative fails to attend any Planning and Zoning Commission meeting or Board of Trustees meeting at which his application appears on the agenda, the commission or Board of Trustees may choose not to take action on the application. 3. For those applications appealed to the Planning and Zoning Commission, and found to conform to all ordinances and codes, the Planning and Zoning Commission shall authorize the Village Clerk- Treasurer or designee to issue the appropriate permit, subject to receipt of State permit, if required. 4. Those applications appealed to the Planning and Zoning Commission and not conforming to all ordinances and codes, shall be disapproved by the Planning and Zoning Commission; the applicant may then pursue a variance or a rezone, or modify the plans to bring them into compliance and resubmit the permit application. 5. The Village Clerk-Treasurer or designee shall inform the applicant of the appropriate procedures and collect applicable fees and expenses. 6. If a variance is requested, the Planning and Zoning Commission shall set a date and conduct a public hearing within the time prescribed by law to adopt findings of fact and conclusions of law for consideration by the Board of Trustees at its next scheduled meeting. Where, by reason of exceptional narrowness, shallowness or shape of a specific piece of property at the time of the original adoption of the regulations or exceptional topographical conditions or other extraordinary or exceptional situation or condition of a specific piece of property where the strict application of this title would result in peculiar and exceptional practical difficulties or exception and undue hardship upon the owner of the property, the commission may make such recommendations as may be appropriate following such hearing to the Board of Trustees by proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law; provided, however, that the owners of all lots within one hundred feet (100'), excluding public rights-of- way shall be notified by certified mail, return receipt requested, of any requests for variance and of the hearing on a request at least fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing on the request for variance by the commission. Such notice shall include information that the hearing shall include the commission acting in its capacity as to recommendations to the Board of Trustees making the final determination and that evidence may be submitted at either stage. For purposes of notification under this section, State Statutes shall be followed. The Board of Trustees may then act upon such recommendations in any manner in which the Board of Trustees may deem appropriate and lawful. Any person or entity making a formal appearance at the public hearing before the commission shall be informed at that Public Hearing that the recommendations of the commission in the matter shall be considered at the next regular meeting of the Board of Trustees and that the Board of Trustees may consider additional evidence as a part of its deliberations. 7. If a rezone is requested, the Board of Trustees shall set a date and conduct a public hearing on the request within the time prescribed by law. If approved and not appealed, the new zone designation becomes effective thirty (30) days after the decision is filed with the Village Clerk-Treasurer. 8. Public hearings, held by the commission or Board of Trustees, shall be conducted in accordance with applicable State law and procedures as recommended by the New Mexico Municipal League ensuring compliance with *Battershell v. City of Albuquerque*, 108 NM 658 (Ct. App. 1989) and an audio record of the hearing shall be made. The commission and Board of Trustees shall allow all amendments to any application which may be necessary in furtherance of justice. Findings of fact and conclusions of law reflecting the final decision of the Board of Trustees shall be filed with the Village Clerk-Treasurer within thirty five (35) days of the conclusion of the hearing before the Board of Trustees. Such findings shall be signed by all members of the Board of Trustees in attendance at the hearing, or by the Mayor if so authorized by all Trustees in attendance; dissenting Trustees must file a written dissenting opinion. Aggrieved parties have thirty (30) days from the filing to file a notice of appeal pursuant to State law, and mail a copy of the notice of appeal to each interested party who appeared at or participated in the hearing. Notice shall be given by U.S. mail, certified return receipt requested. The costs of said notification shall be borne by the appellant. 9. If a Planning and Zoning Commission hearing, not involving a variance, results in an appeal or, if a Planning and Zoning Commission finding, not involving a variance, is appealed, The Village Board of Trustees shall set a date for a public hearing on the appeal within the time prescribed by law. Such appeal shall be de novo before the Board of Trustees conducted as set forth above provided that evidence taken in a hearing before the Planning and Zoning Commission may be considered as original evidence subject to a legal objection, the same as if the evidence was originally offered in the hearing before the Board of Trustees. The Board of Trustees shall allow all amendments which may be necessary in furtherance of justice. Public hearings require a minimum of fifteen (15) days notice. 10. If no appeal is filed pursuant to State law within the time proscribed therein from the time the finding is filed with the Village Clerk-Treasurer, the Village Clerk-Treasurer or his designee shall issue the appropriate permit if an application has been filed and approved. (Ord. 378, 1-9-2018) O. Meeting Minutes: Minutes of each Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, including results of any public hearings, shall be submitted to the Board of Trustees at the next regular Village Council meeting. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) 9-2-4: FEES: A. Rezoning: A fee as set by the Board of Trustees plus required postage for notification and publication costs shall be charged for filing application for rezoning. B. Variance: A fee as set by the Board of Trustees plus required postage for notification and publication costs shall be charged for filing a request for variance. C. Building Site Permit: A fee of ten percent (10%) of the State building permit fee, with a minimum fee set by the Board of Trustees, shall be charged for a building site permit. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) D. Sign And Fence Permit: A fee as set by the Board of Trustees shall be charged for sign and fence permits. (Ord. 277A, 8-10-1999) E. Supplemental Permit: The fee for a supplemental permit shall be half of that of the original permit. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) 9-2-5: AMENDMENTS AND CHANGES: The Village Board of Trustees may, from time to time, on its own motion or on petition, after public notice and hearing at which all parties in interest and citizens shall have an opportunity to be heard, amend the regulations and zones herein established. Notice of the proposed amendment shall be given at least fifteen (15) days in advance of the time and place of the hearing, and shall be published in the same manner within the limits of the Village as set forth by statute for publication of ordinances. Such other notice as may be required by State law shall also be given. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) 9-2-6: BOARD OF APPEALS: A. Established: The Board of Trustees is hereby constituted as a Board of Appeals to hear any appeal made by a person aggrieved by a recommendation of the Planning and Zoning Commission. B. Powers: The Board of Appeals shall have the following powers: 1. To hear and decide appeals where it is alleged there is an error in any determination made in the enforcement of the zoning regulations. 2. Where, by reason of exceptional narrowness, shallowness or shape of a specific piece of property at the time of the original adoption of the regulations or exceptional topographical conditions or other extraordinary or exceptional situation or condition of a specific piece of property, where the strict application of this title would result in peculiar and exceptional practical difficulties or exceptional and undue hardship upon the owner of the property, the Board of Trustees is hereby empowered to authorize a variation from strict application to relieve the difficulties or hardships; provided, however, that the owners of all lots within one hundred feet (100'), excluding public rights-of-way, shall be notified by certified mail, return receipt requested, of any requests for variance and of the hearing on a request at least fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing on the request for variance by the commission as set forth in this title. For purposes of notification under this section, State Statutes shall be followed. (Ord. 378, 1-9-2018) 9-2-7: PENALTY; ENFORCEMENT: A. Penalty: Any person or corporation who shall violate any of the provisions of this title or fail to comply therewith or with any of the requirements thereof, or who shall build or alter any buildings in violation of any detailed statement or plan submitted and approved hereunder, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be liable to a fine of not more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) and/or imprisonment for up to ninety (90) days. Each day such violation shall be permitted to exist shall constitute a separate offense. The owner of any building or premises or part thereof where anything in violation of this title shall be placed or shall exist, and any architect, building contractor, agent, person, or corporation employee in connection therewith and who may have assisted in the commission of any such violation shall be guilty of a separate offense and upon conviction thereof shall be fined and/or imprisoned as hereinabove provided. B. Enforcement Procedure: Any possible violation shall be reported to the Village office. A representative of the Village shall determine if a violation exists. The owner/contractor of the project shall be notified by certified letter of the nature of the violation and what procedures shall be taken to correct same. If no response is received within ten (10) days or if immediate action is necessary, it shall be the responsibility of the Mayor or his representative to enforce the ordinance. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

CHAPTER 3

ZONES

SECTION: 9-3-1: Established 9-3-2: Vacated Land 9-3-3: Double Frontage And Odd Shaped Lots 9-3-4: Recently Annexed Territory 9-3-5: Zoning History By Lot And Description 9-3-1: ESTABLISHED: Zoning regulations as herein set forth are approved and established. The village is hereby divided into zones, which zones were previously known by the titles in parentheses below, except such zones as did not heretofore exist, and shall now be known by the designations set opposite the previous titles as follows: A. Residential zones: - R-1 (A) residential housing. - R-2 (A-M) residential apartments, multiple dwellings. - R-3 (A-T) residential mobile homes, permanently placed. B. Commercial zones: - C-1 (D) offices, banks, hospitals, clinics. - C-2 (D) wholesale and retail. - C-3 (D) automotive and trailer sales. - C-4 (D) light manufacturing. - C-5 car wash. - C-6 automotive repair. C-7 vehicle fueling stations. C-8 facilities serving food and/or beverages. C-9 auto wrecking yards, kennels. C-10 recreation and amusement facilities. C. Recreation and transit accommodation facilities zones: - T-1 (T-1) (D) tourist lodging and eating facilities. - T-2 (T-2) (E) recreational vehicle parks. - T-3 (T-3) (D) stables. - M-1 mobile home parks. D. Greenbelt: - G-1 open space, no structures. - G-2 parks and recreation and related structures. All of such are adopted by action of the board of trustees and filed in the village clerk/treasurer’s office. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997; amd. Ord. 333, 5-10-2005; per correspondence dated 5-12-2009) **9-3-2: VACATED LAND:** Whenever any street, alley or any other public way is vacated by official action of the village, the zones adjoining each side of the street, alley or public way shall be automatically extended to the center of the vacated area, and any area included in the vacation shall then and thenceforth be subject to all appropriate regulations of the extended zones. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-3-3: DOUBLE FRONTAGE AND ODD SHAPED LOTS:** Where any lot abuts two (2) streets which either do not intersect or which intersect at an angle of less than seventy degrees (70°) with reference to the lot: A. Permanent unobstructed open space equal to the zone front yard shall be provided along any side of the lot which abuts a street. B. Setbacks for all odd-shaped lots will be determined by the planning and zoning commission in accordance with the most applicable rule. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-3-4: RECENTLY ANNEXED TERRITORY:** All territory which may hereafter be annexed to the village shall be subject to all of the regulations of zone G-1 (open space, no structures), unless the village board of trustees accepts a zoning plan with the annexation. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-3-5: ZONING HISTORY BY LOT AND DESCRIPTION:** The boundaries of the zoning districts as described in section 9-3-1 of this chapter shall be as set forth in the attachment hereto entitled "Cloudcroft Zoning History By Lots", which attachment and all information thereon are made a part of this title and have the force and effect as if the attachment were fully set forth herein. The attachment, as it may be amended from time to time to reflect zoning changes, shall be on file with the village clerk/treasurer. Any property lying within the boundaries of the village which is not specifically described in the attachment shall be presumed to be zoned R-1. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)
**CHAPTER 4** **RESIDENTIAL ZONES USE REGULATIONS**
**ARTICLE A. R-1 ZONE**
SECTION: 9-4A-1: Uses Permitted 9-4A-2: Structure Per Lot 9-4A-3: Area 9-4A-4: Setback, Height Restrictions **9-4A-1: USES PERMITTED:** A building or premises shall be used only for the following purposes: Accessory buildings as provided in section 9-8-2 of this title. Fences as provided in section 9-8-1 of this title. Golf course. Home occupations. Nonprofit religious, educational and philanthropic institutions, with exceptions of penal or mental institutions. Off street parking as provided in chapter 9 of this title. Preservation of historical sites as provided in ordinance to be adopted or as may be amended. Public park, playground, community building, library. Retaining walls in accordance with the UBC (uniform building code). School, church. Signs as provided in chapter 10 of this title. Single-family dwellings excluding mobile homes. Nightly Rentals in single family dwellings provided the owner or vendor has obtained a Lodger’s Tax License as provided in Section 3-4-6 of the Cloudcroft Village Code. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997; amd. Ord. 385, 1-14-2020) **9-4A-2: STRUCTURE PER LOT:** There shall be only one main structure per lot provided that multiple adjacent and contiguous lots owned by the same person or entity may be treated as one lot provided further that setbacks are observed as set forth herein for multiple adjacent and contiguous lots owned by the same person or entity. (Ord. 336, 8-9-2005) **9-4A-3: AREA:** Every lot shall have an area of not less than four thousand (4,000) square feet, unless a lot having a lesser area than herein required was a lot of record prior to May 5, 1966 (the effective date of ordinance 37). (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-4A-4: SETBACK, HEIGHT RESTRICTIONS:** Setback requirements as specified below are the minimum measurement from the lot line to the physical building and any projections thereof, including any roof overhang that exceeds three feet (3'). Landings forty four inches (44") long having a width not more than the width of the door served with stairs that same width shall not be considered a projection. A. Front Yard: A minimum front yard setback of twenty five feet (25') or twenty five percent (25%) of the depth of the lot, whichever is smaller. B. Side Yard: A minimum side yard setback of seven and one-half feet (7 1/2') along each side lot line. Lots fifty feet (50') or less in width may have a side yard setback of five feet (5'). The side yard on the street side of a corner lot shall be not less than fifteen feet (15') in width. C. Rear Yard: A minimum rear yard setback of thirty feet (30') or twenty percent (20%) of the depth of the entire lot, whichever amount is smaller. D. Height: No part of any building or structure shall exceed thirty five feet (35') in height above grade. (See definition for "grade" set forth in section 9-1-3 of this title.) (Ord. 344, 7-10-2007)

laws.title: Article B. R-2 Zone
laws.content:
SECTION: 9-4B-1: Uses Permitted 9-4B-2: Area 9-4B-3: Density 9-4B-4: Setback, Height Restrictions 9-4B-5: Refuse Area **9-4B-1: USES PERMITTED:** A building or premises shall be used only for the following purposes: Accessory buildings as provided in Section 9-8-2 of this Title. Any use allowed in Zone R-1. Boarding houses. Fences as provided in Section 9-8-1 of this Title. Multiple dwellings, condominiums, apartments, multi-plexes. Off-street parking as provided in Chapter 9 of this Title. Preservation of historical sites as provided in ordinance to be adopted or as may be amended. Retaining walls in accordance with the UBC (Uniform Building Code). Row dwellings, townhouses. Signs as provided in Chapter 10 of this Title. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-4B-3: DENSITY:** If any project or complex intended for development under a common plan exceeds forty five thousand (45,000) square feet of land area, exclusive of public streets and rights of way, the maximum allowable number of dwelling units shall be one per two thousand two hundred fifty (2,250) square feet of land area. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-4B-4: SETBACK, HEIGHT RESTRICTIONS:** Setback requirements as specified below are to be considered the minimum measurement from the lot line to the physical building and any projections thereof, including any roof overhang that exceeds three feet (3'). Landings forty four inches (44") long having a width not more than the width of the door served with stairs that same width shall not be considered a projection. A. Front Yard: A minimum front yard setback of fifteen feet (15') for standard buildings and for complexes where common open space or courtyards are not provided. For projects or complexes in which not more than sixty percent (60%) of the total land area is used for buildings, an eight foot (8') front setback will be allowed. Under the sixty percent (60%) option, the open space shall at no time be diminished. B. Side Yard: 1. A minimum side yard setback of seven and one-half feet ( $7\frac{1}{2}$ ) along each side lot line. 2. On any corner lot, the least width of any side yard along a side street lot line shall be eight feet (8'). 3. For projects or complexes in which not more than sixty percent (60%) of the total land area is used for buildings, a zero side line or common wall will be allowed; providing, however, that the side yard restrictions shall apply to the extreme (end) units in respect to the adjacent street or lot line of ownership other than the proposed project or complex. C. Rear Yard: A minimum ten foot (10') rear yard setback on every lot. D. Height: No part of any building or structure shall exceed thirty feet (30') in height above grade. (See definition for "grade" as set forth in Section 9-1-3 of this Title.) (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-4B-5: REFUSE AREA:** An area for refuse containers shall be provided on the property. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **ARTICLE C. R-3 ZONE** SECTION: **9-4C-1: Uses Permitted** **9-4C-2: Structure Per Lot** **9-4C-1: USES PERMITTED:** A building or premises shall be used only for the following purposes: Accessory buildings as provided in section 9-8-2 of this title. Any use allowed in zone R-1. Fences as provided in section 9-8-1 of this title. Mobile homes, permanently placed, used as a single-family dwelling: All mobile homes in this zone shall be connected to sewer, water and electricity and be set up on a permanent foundation with axles and tongues removed. Only one mobile home shall occupy one lot. Setback, height and lot size restrictions for zone R-3 shall be the same as those for zone R-1, except that mobile homes are restricted to one story in height. (See definitions for "basement", "grade" and "story", as provided in section 9-1-3 of this title.) Minimum floor space shall be six hundred (600) square feet. Mobile homes must be completely skirted. Off street parking as provided in chapter 9 of this title. Preservation of historical sites as provided in ordinance to be adopted or as may be amended.
