laws.title: Permitted Uses
laws.content:
In zone T-2, the property shall be used only for a recreational vehicle park suitable for temporary location of mobile units. Zone T-2 may include the following:

- Accessory buildings as provided in section 9-8-2 of this title except that one service building of no more than six hundred (600) square feet of gross floor area may be constructed even though no main building is located on the premises; such service building must comply with subsections 9-8-2A1 and A3 of this title and shall be used only to accommodate sanitary conveniences, storage facilities, laundry and utility rooms.

- Architecture as required in ordinance 237 (see title 8, chapter 2 of this code), or as may be amended.

- Fences as provided in section 9-8-1 of this title. Note: There shall be a solid fence not less than four feet (4') nor more than six feet (6') in height on any side of the park that abuts property under other ownership, excepting public rights of way, and which shall comply with the requirements for fences in section 9-8-1 of this title.

- Motor homes.

- Off street parking for RV spaces shall be considered included in the individual RV spaces.

- Office unit, one, serving the administrative function of the park which shall comply with zone R-1 requirements and may include the residence of the manager of the park.

- Pickup campers.

- Preservation of historical sites as required in ordinance to be adopted or as may be amended.

- Recreational vehicles (RVs).

- Retaining walls in accordance with the IBC (international building code).

- Signs; one sign not to exceed eight (8) square feet in area which shall comply with the requirements for signs in chapter 10 of this title.

- Tents.

- Trailers, including fifth wheels, pop-up campers. (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Refuse Area
laws.content: An area for refuse containers shall be provided on the property, except that a recreational vehicle park with fewer than six (6) spaces shall be exempt from this requirement. (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Setbacks
laws.content: There shall be a minimum setback of ten feet (10') from a lot line to any RV space or park building, except that the setback for any residence shall comply with R-1 restrictions. The owner shall ensure that no RV, tent, trailer, pickup camper or other occupant of the park encroaches on the area within the setback. (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Height Restrictions
laws.content: A. No part of any building or structure shall exceed one story or twenty feet (20') above grade except for the office unit/residence of the manager as provided in section 9-6B-1 of this article. (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Entrances, Exits Unobstructed
laws.content: Entrances and/or exits from the recreational vehicle park shall be visually unobstructed. (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Village Permit Required
laws.content: The owner of the proposed RV park shall submit, in addition to the requirements of section 9-2-3 of this title, a plan showing RV spaces, fences and utilities (including dump stations). (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Environmental Compliance
laws.content: Each recreational vehicle park shall comply with all rules and regulations of the state of New Mexico environmental division. (Ord. 333, 5-10-2005)

laws.title: Size
laws.content:
Each parking space shall have:

A. Area: Minimum area of one hundred eighty (180) square feet.

B. Width: Minimum width of nine feet (9').

C. Ingress, Egress: Adequate room for ingress and egress.

D. One-Half Units, Measurements: When units or measurements determining the number of required off-street parking and off-street loading spaces result in a number of one-half ( $1/2$ ) or greater, an additional space shall be required.

E. Exceed Twenty; Size Reduction: When the determined number of required parking spaces exceeds twenty (20), ten percent (10%) of the required spaces may measure eight feet by sixteen feet (8' x 16') and be one hundred twenty eight (128) square feet in area for compact vehicles.

F. Handicapped Parking: All commercial zones shall provide handicapped parking in compliance with the current UBC.

G. Snow Removal: Provision for snow removal is the responsibility of the owner. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

laws.title: Parking Spaces Required
laws.content:
Apartments, rooming houses, boarding houses, lodging houses, club and fraternity housing having sleeping rooms, and other multiple dwellings $1\frac{1}{2}$ spaces for each dwelling unit
Automotive and machinery repair, sales or wholesaling 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Banks, businesses or professional offices 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Bowling alleys 4 spaces for each alley
Churches 1 space for each 100 square feet of floor space used for assembly purposes
Hospitals 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Hotels, motels and bed and breakfasts 1 space for each dwelling unit or sleeping unit (see subsection 9-9-4B of this Chapter)
Libraries 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Manufacturing Not less than 1 space for each 800 square feet of gross floor area, plus 1 space for each employee during the maximum shift
Medical and dental clinic 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Mobile home parks 2 spaces per mobile home lot, plus 1 additional space (for guest parking) for every 3 mobile home lots or spaces, all to be provided within the mobile home park area
Motels (see hotels)
Museums and similar nonassembly cultural facilities 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area, or as determined by the Planning and Zoning Commission
Offices not providing customer services or sales on the premises 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Residences (single-family dwellings and permanently placed mobile homes) 2 spaces for each unit
Restaurants and bars 1 space for each 100 square feet of gross floor area
Retail stores, except as otherwise specified herein 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Sanitariums, children’s homes, asylums, nursing homes, etc. 1 space for each 3 beds
Schools: private, vocational, etc. 1 space for each employee and 1 space for each 3 students of driving age
Stadiums, sports arenas, theaters, auditoriums and other places of public assembly, including those on school property, and clubs and lodges having no sleeping quarters 1 space for each 100 square feet of gross floor area used for assembly
Swimming pools, commercial and public 1 space for each 10 persons based on capacity load
Theaters (see stadiums)
Transportation terminals and facilities Adequate number as determined by the Planning and Zoning Commission
Vehicle fueling stations 1 space for each 600 square feet of gross floor area
Warehouse and wholesale storage buildings (dead storage of high volume distribution) 1 space for each employee on the maximum shift, plus 1 (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-9-3: PARKING REQUIREMENTS FOR USES NOT SPECIFIED:** The parking requirements for land uses which are not specified in this chapter shall be determined by the Planning and Zoning Commission. Said determination shall be based upon the requirements for the most comparable use specified herein. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-9-4: GENERAL PROVISIONS:** A. Location: Off street parking facilities shall be located as hereinafter specified: 1. For single-family and duplex dwellings, required parking shall be located on the same lot as the building which it is required to serve. 2. For all other uses, required parking shall be located on the same lot or on an abutting lot. Required parking shall not be located across a public street or with an intervening property, except by conditional use permit approved by the Planning and Zoning Commission. In the event a separately owned lot is utilized, a lease shall be recorded with the Village Clerk-Treasurer. 3. In Commercial Zones C-1, C-2 and C-8, a variance from parking requirements may only be obtained by paying to the Village a fee to be determined by the Village Board of Trustees and based on the number of spaces not provided. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) 4. Burro Avenue retail parking from Glorietta Avenue to Mescalero Avenue/Swallow Place and that fronting Lots 1 through 8 of Block 7 and Lots 1 through 3 of Block 1 of Skywater Subdivision on Village right-of-way, whether acquired through plat dedication or conveyance, will be considered a single parking lot (similar to a shopping mall) shared by all buildings and premises that front these areas. Individual buildings and premises are not required to provide additional off street parking. However, parking space requirements for developments involving more than one lot as such may have been platted on the effective date hereof, and fronting on the area of Burro Avenue from Glorietta Avenue to Mescalero/Swallow Place will be the same as for developments not on Burro Avenue. (Ord. 375, 6-13-2017) B. Mixed Occupancies In Building: In the case of mixed uses in the building or on a lot, the total requirements for off street parking facilities shall be the sum of the requirements for the various uses computed separately. Off street parking facilities for one use shall not be considered as providing required parking facilities for any other use, except as hereinafter specified for joint use. C. Joint Use: The Planning and Zoning Commission may authorize joint use of parking facilities when use of the facilities is primarily daytime for one applicant and nighttime for the other, or weekdays for one applicant and weekends for the other. D. Submission Of Plans: The plans for any proposed commercial parking area shall be submitted to the Planning and Zoning Commission at the time of the application for a building permit for the building to which the parking area is accessory. The plan shall clearly indicate the proposed development, including location, size, shape, design, curb cuts, lighting, landscaping and other features and appurtenances of the proposed parking lot. E. Surface: All off street parking facilities shall be surfaced with base course, concrete, asphaltic concrete, asphalt oil, or any other comparable surfacing and shall be maintained in good condition, free of all weeds, trash and other debris, and shall be properly drained, graded and cleared of snow. F. Entrances And Exits: Entrances and/or exits shall be located at least five feet (5') from any side lot line and at least twenty five feet (25') from the side lot line on the street side of a corner lot. G. Barriers: Wherever required to prevent vehicles using the parking facility from encroaching upon the public streets, alleys or sidewalks, there shall be provided a barrier not less than six inches (6") high. H. Fences: Wherever a commercial parking facility abuts or is directly across the street from any residence or residential zone, such parking facility shall be isolated from such residence or residential zone by the construction of a solid fence not less than four feet (4') nor more than six feet (6') in height. With the approval of the Village, a hedge of suitable variety may be substituted for such fence. I. Lighting: Lighting shall comply with title 8, chapter 3 of this Code. J. Use Restrictions: The parking area shall only be used for passenger vehicles and in no case shall be used for the commercial sale, repair work, storage, dismantling or servicing of any vehicles, equipment, materials or supplies. No vehicle over twenty thousand (20,000) pounds' gross vehicle weight shall be housed in Zones R-1, R-2, R-3, T-1, T-2, M-1, G-1 or G-2. K. Loading Berths: Any commercial establishment shall provide a minimum of one off street loading or unloading space. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **CHAPTER 10**

laws.title: General Provisions
laws.content:
A. **Permit Required**: Any sign which is not exempt shall require a village sign permit.

B. **Illumination**: Exempt signs shall not be illuminated.

C. **Flashing, Moving Lights**: Signs shall not contain, include or be illuminated by any flashing, intermittent or moving lights.

D. **Resembling Official Signs**: Signs shall not imitate or resemble any official traffic sign, signal or device.

E. **Commercial Signs On Trees**: Commercial signs shall not be erected or maintained upon trees.

F. **Painting Signs On Rocks**: Signs shall not be painted or drawn upon rocks or other natural features. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

G. **Upon Village Property**: No sign except temporary unlit exempt signs as described in subsection 9-10-2E of this chapter shall be erected on village property without a license issued by the board of trustees. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003)

H. **Attachment To Utility Poles**: No signs shall be attached to utility poles.

I. **Obscuring Or Obstructing Traffic**: Signs may not be located in such a manner as to obscure or otherwise interfere with the effectiveness of an official traffic sign, signal or device; or to obstruct, interfere with or compromise the safety of vehicular or pedestrian traffic. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

J. **Architecture**: With the exception of temporary unlit exempt signs described in subsections 9-10-2A, C, D, E, F and H of this chapter, all signs in zones C-1 through G-2 shall comply with title 8, chapter 2 of this code. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003)

K. **Lighting**: All signs shall comply with title 8, chapter 3 of this code.

L. **Location Within Lot Line**: All components of a sign shall be located within the lot lines of the lot on which it is erected. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

laws.title: Exempt Signs NOT Requiring Permit
laws.content:
A. **Real Estate Signs**: Real estate signs not exceeding four (4) square feet in area and four feet (4') in height which advertise the sale, rental or lease of the premises upon which they are located. Such signs shall be removed within seven (7) days of the sale, closing, rental or leasing of said property. B. **Residential Name And Street Address Signs**: One residential name and street address sign so long as said sign is no more than two (2) square feet in area and is attached to a structure. Such sign shall not project more than one inch (1") beyond the face of the building. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) C. **Temporary Unlit Banners**: 1. Banner like signs, including, but not limited to, pennants, pennant flap, streamers and fliers advertising a business or other for profit entity, if approved in writing by the village administrator, may be displayed for not more than fourteen (14) days in a twelve (12) month period. 2. Application shall be made on forms provided by the village and submitted to the village administrator who shall refer such application to the planning and zoning commission for comment. Such application shall include a drawing of the sign reflecting color, size, and appearance, as well as the number and proposed location. 3. Such banner like signs shall conform as provided in section 9-10-5 of this chapter and must utilize a western/railroad motif as provided in section 8-2-6 of this code. 4. The village administrator after consideration of the comments by the planning and zoning commission may issue written approval with such conditions as determined to comply with the intent of this exemption with a copy to be kept by the village clerk for at least twenty four (24) months. (Ord. 349, 5-12-2009) D. **Temporary Political Signs**: Temporary unlit political signs shall be permitted up to a total area of six (6) square feet for each premises. Such signs may be erected no earlier than thirty (30) days prior to any primary, general or special election. They shall be removed within three (3) days after the election to which the sign pertains. The candidate portrayed on the sign or for whom the sign advertises shall bear the responsibility for removal. These signs may only be placed on private property and shall not be attached to utility poles. E. Advertising For Community Or Civic Events: Temporary unlit signs advertising community or civic events, and public entertainments presented by, or for the benefit of, nonprofit entities as defined by section 501C3 of the internal revenue code: such signs, if approved in writing by the village administrator, may be erected no earlier than fourteen (14) days prior to the event and shall be removed within three (3) days after the event. Copies of such approval shall be filed with the village clerk/treasurer. The administrator shall regulate the size, number and location of such signs. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) F. Construction Signs: One construction sign on the construction site which does not exceed ten (10) square feet in area. Such signs shall be removed upon completion of the project. G. Memorial Signs Or Tablets: One memorial sign or tablet not exceeding three (3) square feet in area and permanently attached to the building or structure. H. Directional And Informational Signs: Directional and informational signs displaying such legends as "self-service", "parking", "open", "closed", "exit", "entrance", "lounge", "coffee shop", "office", "men's and women's restrooms", "inflammable", including arrows, menus, etc., shall be allowed. Each such sign shall not exceed two (2) square feet. It shall not be permissible for the name of the business to appear on directional signs. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) I. G-2 Public Parks And Recreation Signs: G-2 public parks and recreation signs erected by the village, unlit and not exceeding sixteen (16) square feet in area. (Ord. 277A, 8-10-1999) 9-10-3: ZONES R-1 AND R-3 SIGNS: Only the following exempt unlit signs shall be allowed in zones R-1 and R-3: A. Real Estate Signs: Real estate signs not exceeding four (4) square feet in area and four feet (4') in height which advertise the sale, rental or lease of the premises upon which they are located. Such signs shall be removed within seven (7) days of the sale, closing, rental or leasing of said property. B. Residential Name And Street Address Signs: One residential name and street address sign so long as said sign is no more than two (2) square feet in area and is attached to a structure. Such sign shall not project more than one inch (1") beyond the face of the building. C. Temporary Political Signs: Temporary political signs shall be permitted up to a total area of six (6) square feet for each premises. Such signs may be erected no earlier than thirty (30) days prior to any primary, general or special election. They shall be removed within three (3) days after the election to which the sign pertains. The candidate portrayed on the sign or for whom the sign advertises shall bear the responsibility for removal. These signs may only be placed on private property and shall not be attached to utility poles. D. Construction Signs: One construction sign on the construction site which does not exceed ten (10) square feet in area. Such signs shall be removed upon completion of the project. E. Memorial Signs Or Tablets: One memorial sign or tablet not exceeding three (3) square feet in area and permanently attached to the building or structure. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) 9-10-4: ZONE R-2 SIGNS: A. Allowable Signs: Only the following exempt unlit signs shall be allowed in zone R-2: 1. Real Estate Signs: Real estate signs not exceeding four (4) square feet in area and four feet (4') in height which advertise the sale, rental or lease of the premises upon which they are located. Such signs shall be removed within seven (7) days of the sale, closing, rental or leasing of said property. 2. Residential Name And Street Address Signs: One residential name and street address sign so long as said sign is no more than two (2) square feet in area and is attached to a structure. Such sign shall not project more than one inch (1") beyond the face of the building. 3. Temporary Political Signs: Temporary political signs shall be permitted up to a total area of six (6) square feet for each premises. Such signs may be erected no earlier than thirty (30) days prior to any primary, general or special election. They shall be removed within three (3) days after the election to which the sign pertains. The candidate portrayed on the sign or for whom the sign advertises shall bear the responsibility for removal. These signs may only be placed on private property and shall not be attached to utility poles. 4. Construction Signs: One construction sign on the construction site which does not exceed ten (10) square feet in area. Such sign shall be removed upon completion of the project. 5. Memorial Signs Or Tablets: One memorial sign or tablet not exceeding three (3) square feet in area and permanently attached to the building or structure. B. Business Sign; Nameplate: One business sign or nameplate requiring a village sign permit and not exceeding eight (8) square feet in area shall be permitted listing the name of the structure. This sign may be either attached to a structure or freestanding. The bottom of a freestanding sign shall be no more than one foot (1') above the ground. C. Obscuring Or Obstructing Traffic: Signs may not be located in such a manner as to obscure or otherwise interfere with the effectiveness of an official traffic sign, signal or device, or to obstruct or interfere with or compromise the safety of vehicular or pedestrian traffic. D. Illumination: Illuminated signs shall be lighted in such a way that the light source cannot be seen from the street or adjoining property and shall comply with title 8, chapter 3 of this code. E. Location Within Lot Lines: All components of a sign shall be located within the lot lines of the lot on which it is erected. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-10-5: COMMERCIAL ZONE SIGNS (C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6, C-7, C-8, C-9, C-10, G-2, T-1, T-2, M-1):** A. Signs Attached To Structures: 1. The total signage on any single face of a structure shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the area of that face. 2. No roof signs shall be allowed. 3. Illuminated signs shall be lighted in such a way that the light source cannot be seen from the street or adjoining property and shall comply with title 8, chapter 3 of this code. 4. All signs shall comply with title 8, chapter 2 of this code. B. Freestanding Signs: Signs not attached to the face of a structure shall be considered freestanding and shall comply with the following: 1. Only one freestanding sign shall be allowed on each lot. 2. Gasoline price signs; service stations shall be permitted one double faced, on site sign not to exceed twelve (12) square feet per face and five feet (5') in height advertising the price of gasoline. Such signs may be freestanding so long as all of the criteria for a freestanding sign are met. Such signs shall not contain any advertisement other than brand name. The height limitation referred to above shall not apply to those gas price signs which are mounted on a freestanding sign. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) 3. The maximum area for any one freestanding sign shall be thirty two (32) square feet where the height will not exceed the width of the actual sign, with a maximum height of six feet (6'), including border and trim, whether on a post or base from the ground elevation to its highest point. (Ord. 365, 9-10-2013) 4. The area shall be measured by the smallest square, rectangle, triangle, circle or combination thereof which will encompass the entire sign. 5. Freestanding signs may be placed back to back, side to side, stacked or in V-type construction with not more than two (2) displays to each facing. Such sign structure or structures shall be considered one sign. 6. Signs may not be located in such a manner as to obscure or otherwise interfere with the effectiveness of an official traffic sign, signal or device; or to obstruct, interfere with or compromise the safety of vehicular or pedestrian traffic. 7. All components of a sign shall be located within the lot lines of the lot on which it is erected. 8. Illuminated signs shall comply with title 8, chapter 3 of this code. 9. Commercial zone signs shall comply with title 8, chapter 2 of this code. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997) **9-10-6: FEES:** The board of trustees may establish fees to be submitted with all applications for signs submitted to the village in accordance with the building permit provisions of this title. (Ord. 277, 10-29-1997)

CHAPTER 11

CONTINUING USES

SECTION: 9-11-1: Continuing Uses **9-11-1: CONTINUING USES:** The lawful use of any premises existing on the effective date of Ordinance 277 may be continued although the use does not conform with the provisions hereof. However, if a nonconforming use has been changed to a more restricted use or a conforming use, it shall not thereafter be returned to a less restricted use. Additions or alterations may be added to such structures without a variance, provided the original structure location on the ground is maintained and no other setback requirement is violated. (Ord. 277A, 8-10-1999)

CHAPTER 12

VARIANCES

SECTION: 9-12-1: Procedure For Variance 9-12-1: PROCEDURE FOR VARIANCE: When a variance from a zoning regulation is requested, notice of a public hearing shall be both published and mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the owners of all lots within one hundred feet (100'), excluding public right-of-way, of the property requesting the variance and the notice shall state that written protests will be reviewed and considered if received in the Village offices by twelve o'clock (12:00) noon of the working day prior to the scheduled public hearing. The notice shall also state that any public hearing for a variance shall be conducted before the commission and the Board of Trustees as set forth in this Code. This notice shall be published and mailed at least fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the hearing. If the owners of twenty percent (20%) or more of the area of those lots protest in writing by twelve o'clock (12:00) noon on the workday prior to the scheduled hearing, the variance shall not become effective unless the variance is approved by a majority vote of all the members of the Board of Trustees. (Ord. 378, 1-9-2018) **TITLE 10** **SUBDIVISION REGULATIONS**¹ **CHAPTER 1** **GENERAL PROVISIONS** SECTION: 10-1-1: Territorial Coverage 10-1-2: General Procedures 10-1-3: Compliance With State Law 10-1-4: Fees For Application Notes ¹ 1. NMSA § 3-20-1 et seq. 10-1-1: TERRITORIAL COVERAGE: These subdivision regulations shall apply to all subdivisions within the subdivision and platting jurisdiction of the Village as provided by County and State law. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) 10-1-2: GENERAL PROCEDURES: A. Compliance Required: It shall be unlawful for anyone to create a subdivision within the territorial coverage of the Village unless by plat, plan and contract in accordance with the laws of the State and this Title. B. Steps: The subdivider will follow these steps (unless qualified and granted permission to follow the alternate procedures listed in Section 10-3-4 of this Title): 1. Step 1: The subdivider shall provide preliminary data (Section 10-3-1 of this Title) and shall comply with the preliminary procedure (Section 10-3-2 of this Title); 2. Step 2: At its next meeting, the Planning and Zoning Commission will review and examine the written, platted and oral information provided by the subdivider and make a recommendation to the Board of Trustees. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) 3. Step 3: The Board of Trustees will approve or disapprove the plan and preliminary plat. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999; amd. 2000 Code) 4. Step 4: If approval is given, the final plat (Section 10-3-3 of this Title) shall be submitted within six (6) months to the Planning and Zoning Commission for its final approval and recommendation to the Board of Trustees. 5. Step 5: The Board of Trustees will approve or disapprove the final plat and plan. (With the approval of the Planning and Zoning Commission, the subdivider may elect to combine the preliminary and final procedures, Steps 1 and 4.) 6. Step 6: Once the final plat has been approved by the Board, the subdivider shall enter into a contract with the Village (Section 10-4-1 of this Title). 7. Step 7: Once the contract has been agreed to and signed by the subdivider and the Village, the subdivider shall file and record the final plat with the County Clerk. No construction, including excavation or earth work, shall take place until the final plat has been filed and recorded with the County Clerk. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) **10-1-3: COMPLIANCE WITH STATE LAW:** The procedures established by State law for approval of subdivisions shall be followed in all cases by the subdivider and the Board of Trustees. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) **10-1-4: FEES FOR APPLICATION:** Prior to the submission of a final plat to the Board of Trustees, the subdivider shall pay to the Village a subdivision application fee to be determined by the Board of Trustees. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999)
**CHAPTER 2** **DEFINITIONS**
SECTION: **10-2-1: Definitions** **10-2-1: DEFINITIONS:** As used in this Title, the following words and terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this Section: **AVAILABLE WASTEWATER TREATMENT CAPACITY:** Current capacity of existing wastewater treatment plant less the current average influent in gallons per day as determined by averaging the measurements of daily influent over the month of July for the previous two (2) years. **CUL-DE-SAC:** A street with only one outlet culminated by a turnaround. **EASEMENT:** A grant from the property owner for the use, for specific purposes, of a strip of land by the general public, or a certain person or persons, or a corporation. **FULL PUMPING CAPACITY:** Average the number of gallons that could be pumped per day over the month of July for each July for the previous five (5) years (all wells running at maximum sustainable flow for 24 hours per day and all spring water continuously collected). **IMMEDIATE FAMILY MEMBER:** Husband, wife, father, stepfather, mother, stepmother, brother, stepbrother, sister, stepsister, son, stepson, daughter, stepdaughter, grandson, stepgrandson, granddaughter, stepgranddaughter, nephew and niece, whether related by natural birth or adoption. **PERFORMANCE BOND:** A surety bond made out to the Village of Cloudcroft in an amount equal to the estimated full cost of the improvements; the cost being estimated by a New Mexico licensed engineer retained by the subdivider and under direction and control of the Village, with full approval of the Village, and said surety bond being legally sufficient to secure to the Village of Cloudcroft that the said improvements will be constructed accordance with regulations as stated in the contract. **PLAT OR REPLAT:** A map, chart, survey or plan certified by a licensed professional surveyor which contains a description of subdivided land with ties to permanent survey monuments. **SUBDIVIDER:** Any person who creates or who has created a subdivision individually or as part of a common promotional plan or any person engaged in the sale, lease or other conveyance of subdivided land. However, "subdivider" does not include licensed real estate brokers acting on another's account. **SUBDIVISION:** The division of a surface area of land, including land within a previously approved subdivision, into two (2) or more parcels by plating or by metes and bounds for the purpose of sale, lease or other conveyance or for building development. However, "subdivision" does not include: A. Division of land created by court order where the order creates no more that one parcel per party; B. Division of land resulting only in the alteration of parcel boundaries where parcels are altered for the purpose of increasing or reducing the size of contiguous parcels and where the number of parcels is not increased; C. Division of land to create a parcel that is sold or donated as a gift to an immediate family member; however, this exception shall be limited to allow the seller or donor to sell or give no more than one parcel per tract of land per immediate family member; D. Division of land created to provide security for mortgages, liens or deeds of trust; provided, that the division of land is not the result of a seller-financed transaction. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999; amd. 2000 Code)
**CHAPTER 3** **PLAT PROCEDURES**
SECTION: 10-3-1: Preliminary Data Requirements 10-3-2: Preliminary Procedure 10-3-3: Final Plat 10-3-4: Alternate Procedure 10-3-5: Water Rights

laws.title: Preliminary Data Requirements
laws.content:
For subdivision located within the village limits, the supporting documentation required before the preliminary plat is submitted shall provide sufficient information for the village to determine:

A. Water: That sufficient potable water and sufficient pumping and/or collection capacity at the water source will be available to meet the peak daily demand flow rate (as measured by the peak daily discharge from the potable water storage tanks) that has occurred during the previous three (3) year period, plus the demand anticipated (at 600 gallons per lot per day) from the subdivision when fully occupied.

B. Wastewater Plant Capacity: That the capacity of the wastewater treatment plant facilities will be sufficient to meet peak daily water treatment demands (as determined by the peak daily influent that has occurred during the previous 3 year period), plus the demand anticipated (at 300 gallons per day per lot) from the subdivision when fully occupied.

C. Single-Family Dwelling Assumption: All lots shall be assumed to be used for single-family dwelling. If multi-family dwellings or other types of units are to be constructed within the subdivision, then equivalency of single-family units shall be used in the calculation of the eighty percent (80%) limit. If other than single-family units, all capacity must be calculated pursuant to the impact fee ordinance. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999)

laws.title: Final Plat
Alternate Procedure
Water Rights
laws.content:
A. Any subdivider of land not located within the original place of Cloudcroft as shown on the original plat map filed of record, prior to the approval of a final plat, shall be required to transfer to the village of Cloudcroft sufficient water rights to serve all lots in the subdivision being presented for approval.

B. "Sufficient water rights" shall be defined as the right to divert from either surface or underground sources at least 0.45 acre-feet per annum per lot.

C. Such water rights to be acceptable to the village must have been accepted for filing as prima facie evidence of such right with the state engineer of the state of New Mexico.

D. Such water rights shall be deemed to be acceptable when the state engineer of the state of New Mexico has recognized or authorized a transfer of such water rights the place of diversion, change of purpose of use to municipal so that such water rights may be incorporated and used in the Cloudcroft municipal water system by diversion from a surface source or a completed functional well for diversion from an underground basin.

E. In lieu of a transfer of water rights, the subdivider may pay to the village four thousand five hundred dollars ($4,500.00) for each lot. (Ord. 348, 4-14-2009)

laws.title: Contract Required
laws.content:
The subdivider shall be required to enter into a contract with the village, agreeing to abide by and to comply with his layout and drawings, as finally approved, and also all plans and specifications as approved, which contract shall be reviewed annually and shall contain, among other provisions, the following: A. Repairs; Replacement: The subdivider shall be responsible for all repairs to his construction work and the replacement of defective material or workmanship on public property which may become apparent for a period of one year after work has been completed and accepted by the village. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) B. Water, Sewer Lines: For subdivisions within the village limits, the subdivider shall agree to supply and install all water lines and sewer lines of approved weight and quality within the subdivision in accordance with village standards, and also outside of the subdivision a sufficient distance to connect with the village sewer and water system, and to furnish and install approved weight and quality valves, fire hydrants, manholes, manhole rings and covers with sewer stub outs and all appurtenances to the water and sewer systems. Fire hydrants shall have a minimum of a four foot (4') radius clearance on all sides; fire hydrants set into a bank shall have a wall or other device to prevent rubble, dirt and runoff from collecting around them. Fire hydrants shall be located so that the difference in grade between the hydrant and the adjacent improved road is no greater than one foot (1'); the dirt level at the hydrant shall be just below the mounting flange of the hydrant body. Subdivisions outside the village limits but within the planning and platting jurisdiction of the village shall provide an adequate supply of potable water to each lot by a water system approved by the environment department (ED), but not from water sources/aquifers within the village water rights area, without village approval. Subdivisions outside the village limits but within the planning and platting jurisdiction of the village shall connect to a public sanitary sewer system if feasible. Where lots cannot be connected with a public sewer system provisions must be made for sanitary sewerage treatment consisting of a central treatment plant whose discharge meets all federal, state and local standards and does not have the potential for contaminating the village ground and surface water supply. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) C. Additional Water, Sewer Lines: Should the present sewer and water lines and related appurtenances serving a subdivision within the village limits not be adequate as determined by the village, the subdivider shall agree to bear the cost of additional and/or replacement lines and appurtenances thereto in order to carry the increased load made necessary by the subdivision. D. Flood Protection: The subdivider shall agree to protect drainage structures, to build bridges, culverts and other drainage facilities in the area that may be necessary to protect the subdivision, the village and other lands in the area from floods because of the development, and shall not change the existing drainage patterns and quantities for any area outside of the subdivision. E. Damaged Facilities Repaired: Any damage caused by the subdivider to existing water lines, sewer lines and/or any other infrastructure shall be repaired at the subdivider’s expense. F. Licensed Engineer: The subdivider shall agree to retain and pay for the services of a competent New Mexico licensed engineer to inspect all work as the same progresses, make reports to the village, and certify in writing that all work is in compliance with accepted engineering standards; the engineer shall be under the direction and control of the village. G. Performance Bond: The board of trustees shall require the subdivider to post a performance bond in the full amount of one hundred percent (100%) of his projected costs of development using a standard performance bond. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) H. Other Required Documents: A set of as built plans, and such other certificates, affidavits, endorsements or deductions as may be required by the board of trustees to ensure compliance with these regulations. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) **10-4-2: DISCLOSURE STATEMENT:** The subdivider shall give to persons acquiring an interest in the subdivided land a statement complying with the requirements of New Mexico Statutes Annotated section 47-6-17. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999)
**CHAPTER 5** **IMPROVEMENTS; STANDARDS**
**SECTION:** 10-5-1: Utilities Required 10-5-2: Streets 10-5-3: Public Sites And Open Spaces **10-5-1: UTILITIES REQUIRED:** All utilities, including water, sewer, electric transmission lines and street improvements, shall be completed before any building permits shall be issued. Utility design and construction shall be approved by the village and appropriate utility providers. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) **10-5-2: STREETS:** It is hereby required that all dedicated streets shall be a minimum of fifty feet (50') in width, shall be cleared a minimum of twenty four feet (24') in width, and shall be finished or paved a minimum of twenty two feet (22') in width. In lieu of paving in a residential development, streets must have a minimum depth of base course of four inches (4") after compaction with proper drainage. Commercial subdivisions and commercial areas within subdivisions shall be paved. Streets shall be constructed to New Mexico highway department standards to include proper drainage. Street design and construction shall be approved by the village. Streets which terminate in a cul-de-sac shall be no longer than five hundred feet (500'); the terminus shall have a minimum surfaced area radius of fifty feet (50'). Subdivider shall install street signs, of a style selected by the village, at all intersections and such other sites as may be determined by the village. (Ord. 322, 10-14-2003) **10-5-3: PUBLIC SITES AND OPEN SPACES:** A. Dedication For Park, Playground And Similar Spaces: Where a proposed park, playground, school or other public use shown in a general community or master plan is located in whole or in part in a proposed subdivision, the board of trustees may require the dedication or reservation of such area, and in cases of parks, the village shall develop the park within a reasonable time after the subdivision has been completed. However, the subdivider shall not be required to dedicate more than five percent (5%) of the total area of the subdivision to the village for public use, exclusive of streets and alleys. B. Other Areas: Where deemed essential by the board of trustees, upon consideration of the particular type of development proposed in the subdivision, and especially in large scale neighborhood unit developments, the board of trustees may require the dedication or reservation of such other areas or sites of a character, extent and location suitable to the needs created by such development for schools, parks and other neighborhood purposes. However, the subdivider shall not be required to dedicate more than five percent (5%) of the total area of the subdivision to the village for public use, exclusive of streets and alleys. C. Pedestrian Easement: Any subdivision with a common boundary with a national forest, or U.S. government or New Mexico state owned land, shall provide a pedestrian easement every one-half ($^{1}/_{2}$) mile along the property line shared by the subdivision and the public land. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999)
**CHAPTER 6** **VARIANCES**
**SECTION:** 10-6-1: Authority 10-6-2: Conditions Imposed **10-6-1: AUTHORITY:** Where the Board of Trustees finds that extraordinary hardships may result from strict compliance with these regulations, it may vary the regulations so that substantial justice may be done and the public interest secured; provided, that the variation will not have the effect of nullifying the intent and purpose of this Title. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) 10-6-2: CONDITIONS IMPOSED: In granting variances and modifications, the Board of Trustees may require conditions that will, in its judgment, secure substantially the objectives of the standard or requirements so varied or modified. (Ord. 287, 3-9-1999) **CHAPTER 7** **DEVELOPMENT FEE** SECTION: - 10-7-1: General Provisions - 10-7-2: Advisory Committee - 10-7-3: Assumptions; Plan - 10-7-4: Plan; Calculation Of Fee - 10-7-5: Notice; Public Hearing - 10-7-6: Accounting **10-7-1: GENERAL PROVISIONS:** A. State Law; Definitions: There is imposed in the Village a development fee pursuant to laws 1993, chapter 122, and all definitions in such Act are adopted herein and to which reference herein is made as State law. B. Territorial Coverage: The development fee shall be assessed on any new development of property within the Village limits. C. Purpose: The development fee is imposed to pay the following specified costs of constructing capital improvements or facility expansions as authorized by State law. D. Assessment And Collection: The development fee shall be assessed and collected as provided by State law. (Ord. 288, 3-9-1999) **10-7-2: ADVISORY COMMITTEE:** Prior to adoption of a development fee, the Board of Trustees shall appoint a Capital Improvements Advisory Committee, to be composed of not less than five (5) members who shall be appointed by a majority vote of the Board of Trustees. Not less than forty percent (40%) of the membership of the Advisory Committee must be representative of the real estate, development or building industries. No members shall be employees or officials of a municipality or county or other governmental entity. The Advisory Committee serves in an advisory capacity and shall: A. Advise and assist the Board of Trustees in adopting land use assumptions; B. Review the capital improvements plan and file written comments; C. Monitor and evaluate implementation of the capital improvements plan; D. File annual reports with respect to the progress of the capital improvements plan and report to the Board of Trustees any perceived inequities in implementing the plan or imposing the development fee; E. Advise the Board of Trustees of the need to update or revise the land use assumptions, capital improvements plan and development fee. (Ord. 288, 3-9-1999) **10-7-3: ASSUMPTIONS; PLAN:** A. Adoption Of Plan: Upon adoption of land use or system-wide assumptions, the Village shall provide for a capital improvements plan to be developed by qualified professionals using generally accepted engineering and planning practices in accordance with State law. B. Public Hearing: Upon completion of the capital improvements plan, the Board of Trustees shall schedule and publish notice of a public hearing to discuss the adoption of the capital improvements plan and imposition of the development fee with notice as provided by State law. C. Consolidation: The Board of Trustees may consolidate the land use assumption and capital improvements as provided by State law. D. Updating: The Board of Trustees shall update the land use assumptions and capital improvements plan at least every five (5) years, and shall review and evaluate its current land use assumptions and shall cause an update of the capital improvements plan to be prepared and hold hearings in accordance with State law. (Ord. 288, 3-9-1999) **10-7-4: PLAN; CALCULATION OF FEE:** A qualified professional shall prepare the capital improvements plan and calculate the development fee in accordance with State law. The capital improvements plan shall follow the infrastructure capital improvement planning guidelines established by the Department of Finance and Administration and shall address the following: A. Description Of Existing Improvements: A description, as needed to reasonably support the proposed development fee, which shall be prepared by a qualified professional, of the existing capital improvements within the service area and the costs to upgrade, update, improve, expand or replace the described capital improvements to adequately meet existing needs and usage and strict safety, efficiency, environmental or regulatory standards; B. Analysis Of Capacity: An analysis, which shall be prepared by a qualified professional, of the total capacity, the level of current usage and commitments for usage of capacity of the existing capital improvements; C. Description Of Expansions; Costs: A description, which shall be prepared by a qualified professional, of all of the parts of the capital improvements or facility expansions and their costs necessitated by and attributable to new development in the service area based on the approved land use assumptions; D. Table Of Level, Quantity: A definitive table establishing the specific level or quantity of use, consumption, generation or discharge of a service unit for each category of capital improvements or facility expansions and an equivalency or conversion table establishing the ratio of a service unit to various types of land uses, including residential, commercial and industrial; E. Number Of Projected Service Units: The total number of projected service units necessitated by and attributable to new development within the service area based on the approved land use assumption and calculated in accordance with generally accepted engineering or planning criteria; F. Projected Demand: The projected demand for capital improvements or facility expansions required by new service units accepted over a reasonable period of time, not to exceed ten (10) years. (Ord. 288, 3-9-1999) **10-7-5: NOTICE; PUBLIC HEARING:** To impose the development fee, the Village shall schedule and publish notice of a public hearing, pursuant to the Village open meetings resolution to consider land use assumptions, or system-wide land use assumptions, within the designated service area that will be used to develop the capital improvements plan, which public hearing shall be held and conducted in accordance with State law. (Ord. 288, 3-9-1999) **10-7-6: ACCOUNTING:** All money collected through the adoption of a development fee shall be maintained in separate interest-bearing accounts clearly identifying the payor and the category of capital improvements or facility expansions within the service area for which the fee was adopted with interest earned on development fees to become part of the account on which it is earned and subject to all restrictions placed on the use of development fees under State law. An annual report describing the amount of any development fees collected, encumbered and used during the preceding year by category of capital improvement and service area identified as provided shall be a part of the annual audit process. Disbursement from the separate accounts shall be made in accordance with State law. (Ord. 288, 3-9-1999)

laws.title: Grant of Authority
laws.content: There is hereby granted by the village of Cloudcroft, hereinafter called the "village" to Tularosa Basin Telephone Company, its successors and assigns, hereinafter called the "company", the nonexclusive right and privilege to construct, erect, operate and maintain, in, upon, along, across, above, over and under the streets, alleys, public ways and public places now in use or dedicated, and all extensions thereof, and additions thereto, in said village, poles, wires, cables, underground conduits, manholes and other telecommunications facilities necessary or proper for the maintenance and operation in said village of Cloudcroft of the company's telecommunications business; provided, however, that no poles or other facilities shall be placed where the same will interfere with any street, roadway or traffic control facilities or with any existing utility facilities and shall be placed in such a manner as to cause a minimum interference with the rights or reasonable convenience of property owners who adjoin any of said streets, alleys or public ways and places. Any and all changes made by the company for company reasons in the location of the poles, wires, cables, underground conduits, manholes and other telecommunications facilities shall not require the village to pay for the change in any street, roadway or traffic control facility caused by the change of the locations by the company. The cost thereof shall be paid by the company. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Company Liability
laws.content: The company shall, at all times during the life of this franchise, be subject to all lawful exercise of the police power by the village and to such regulations as the village may, by resolution or ordinance, hereafter provide. It is expressly understood and agreed by and between the company and village that the company shall save the village harmless from all loss sustained by the village on account of any suit, judgment, execution, claim or demand whatsoever, resulting from negligence on the part of the company in the construction or maintenance of its telecommunications system in the village. The village shall notify the company's representative in writing at P.O. Box 550, Tularosa, NM 88352, within ten (10) days after the service of process in a suit against the village on account of any negligence as aforesaid on the part of the company. Failure to promptly notify the company as required above shall operate as release of the company's obligation to save the village harmless regarding the claim or demand if such failure of notice results in substantial harm to the company. The village will forward a copy of any notice of claim made under the state tort claims act involving the company within a reasonable period of time. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: House Moving and Other Unusual USE
laws.content: Any person or corporation desiring to move a building or other structure along, or to make any unusual use of, the streets, alleys and public ways of the village which shall interfere with the poles, wires or facilities of the company or the village, shall first give notice to the company or the village, as the case may be, and a sum sufficient to cover the expense and damages incident to the cutting, altering and moving of the wires or other facilities of the company or the village, and before a permit is given by the village therefor, the applicant shall present a receipt from the company showing the payment. Thereupon the company, upon presentation of said permit, shall within a reasonable time thereafter provide for and do such cutting, altering and moving of said wires and facilities as may be necessary to allow such moving or other unusual use of the streets, alleys and public ways of the village. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Tree Trimming
laws.content: The company shall have the authority, to the extent that the village has such authority, to trim trees upon or overhanging streets, highways, alleys, bridges or other public ways or places of the village in order to prevent the branches of such trees from coming in contact with the wires, cables, conductors or other facilities or equipment of the company; provided, however, that the company shall obtain permission of any landowner should it be necessary to trim any tree where the main trunk is located on private property. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Consideration
laws.content: As a further consideration for this franchise, the company shall pay to the village franchise payments in an amount equal to three percent (3%) of the gross monthly recurring revenues, exclusive of all federal and state excise taxes, from the services listed in section 11-1-16, "Appendix A", of this chapter, furnished to subscribers of the company, not including uncollectible revenues related to those services within the village of Cloudcroft. Payment shall be made in quarterly installments within sixty (60) days after the end of each calendar quarter during the term of this franchise. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Inspection of Books
laws.content: The village shall have the right, at all reasonable times, to inspect the books and records of the company pertaining to the company's gross monthly recurring revenues from the services listed in section 11-1-16, "Appendix A", of this chapter received from the company's subscribers located within the limits of the village. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Payment in Lieu of Other Taxes
laws.content: In consideration of the franchise payments hereinabove provided for, it is expressly understood and agreed by the company and the village that these payments shall be in lieu of any and all other franchise, license, occupation or other forms of excise or revenue taxes based upon or measured by the revenues, employees, payroll, property, facilities or equipment of the company, excepting, however, general ad valorem property taxes, special assessments for local improvements and sales or gross receipts taxes (all hereinafter referred to as "excepted taxes"). The franchise payments shall continue only so long as the company is not prohibited from making the payments by any lawful authority having jurisdiction in the premises. Furthermore, if the village does levy, charge or collect or attempt to levy, charge or collect any other franchise, license, occupation or other form of excise or revenue taxes of the type above specified in this paragraph (other than excepted taxes), the obligation to make franchise payments hereunder shall be abated to the extent such other taxes are levied, charged or collected by the village. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Representation of NO Claims Under Prior Franchise
laws.content: The village and the company recognize the existence of and validity of ordinances 338 and 338A, previously granting a franchise to Tularosa Basin Telephone Company ("company"), and agree that the prior franchise has been extended by mutual agreement in order to negotiate this agreement, it being the intent and understanding that there are no claims by the village against Tularosa Basin Telephone Company or the company and no claims by Tularosa Basin Telephone Company or the company against the village with respect to the locations, establishment, construction, maintenance or operation of the company's lines and facilities within the village, or amounts due to the village under the prior franchise. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Notices
laws.content: Written notice to the village shall be sent to Mayor, Village Of Cloudcroft at P.O. Box 817, Cloudcroft, NM 88317. Written notice to the company shall be sent to General Manager, Tularosa Basin Telephone Company, P.O. Box 550, Tularosa, NM 88352. Hand delivery is acceptable. However, receipt shall be acknowledged. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Annexation
laws.content: Upon any annexation of territory to the village, any gross monthly recurring revenues from the services listed in section 11-1-16, "Appendix A", of this chapter received from subscribers located within the annexed area listed shall be included in the base for computation of payments due to the village. Such inclusion shall be effective thirty (30) days after written notice to the company of such annexation is delivered by the village to the company. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)

laws.title: Nonwaiver of Other Rights
laws.content: It is expressly understood and agreed by and between the village and the company that neither the grant nor acceptance of this franchise shall constitute a waiver, either upon the part of the company or the village, of any rights or claims had or made by either with respect to the occupancy of the streets, alleys and public places of the village, under the constitution and laws of the state of New Mexico, nor shall anything herein in any way prejudice or impair any rights or claims existing independently of this franchise of the village or the company, or its predecessors or successors, with respect to the construction, operation and maintenance, either before or after the life of this franchise, of a telecommunications system in the village. (Ord. 371, 3-15-2016)
